verdict.rationale: Rootly documents an official MCP server that exposes incident data and actions as tools to any MCP-compatible client, including Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Code and Gemini CLI. The docs name specific tools such as find_related_incidents and say tools are generated from the OpenAPI spec, and a probe confirms the MCP server docs page exists. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of connecting an agent and using the tools.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect an agent via an official MCP server

citations.quote: The Rootly MCP Server implements the Model Context Protocol to expose Rootly incident data and actions as tools that any MCP-compatible client can use.
you can query incidents, check on-call schedules, find similar past incidents, and take action — all from within Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, or any other MCP-compatible environment.
The server dynamically generates tools from Rootly's OpenAPI specification, so it always reflects the current API surface.
